[F006] I've implemented F006 — the `dontpanic doctor` upgrade-readiness CLI integration as a strictly read-only render. The implementation wires F005's `assemble_upgrade_report` into doctor through a single shared seam (`build_upgrade_report` in `scripts/dontpanic_doctor.py`) that loads the packaged manifest, reads the marker via `read_upgrade_state` (never `write_upgrade_state`, D015), and only fetches under the explicit `--check-upstream` opt-in (D016): plain doctor now appends exactly one `upgrade-readiness` CheckResult (a WARN with pending required/advisory counts + an upstream-behind note + the remediation command when anything pends, else OK), `--upgrade` prints the full human report led by the version/update + upstream summary with each required *and* advisory action's `introduced_commands` (D022/D033), and `--upgrade --json` emits the machine-readable report (`summary` incl. `upstream` + `required[]`/`advisory[]`/`migration_status[]`). I added the `--upgrade`/`--check-upstream` flags to both `dontpanic_doctor.main()` and the public `dontpanic doctor` wrapper in `cli.py` (D053), strapping the advisory `upgrade-readiness` probe out of the strict-exit computation in both surfaces so a pending upgrade never escalates the exit code. A new 11-test file (`test_doctor_upgrade_render_f006.py`) covers the WARN/OK render, JSON shape, no-implicit-fetch default vs `--check-upstream` opt-in, the no-marker-write invariant, introduced_commands on both lists in human+JSON, and an end-to-end
